The (Ga,Fe)N layers contain γ'-GayFe4-yN nanocrystals, with the size of the nanocrystals estimated to be 22±2 nm along the growth direction.
Sample A contains both α-Fe and γ'-GayFe4-yN nanocrystals, while Sample B and the annealed Sample A* (A*) contain only the γ'-GayFe4-yN nanocrystals.
The magnetic response of the samples is dominated by a superparamagnetic-like behavior and a paramagnetic contribution from dilute substitutional Fe3+ ions in the matrix.

The resistivity of all samples increases with decreasing temperature, exhibiting an Arrhenius-type conduction mechanism down to 50K, and a Mott variable range hopping (VRH) conduction mechanism at lower temperatures.
The transition from Arrhenius to Mott VRH conduction occurs between 50-25K for Samples A, A*, and GaN, while it shifts to 130-100K for the capped Sample B.

The Mott hopping temperature T0Mott is two orders of magnitude lower in the GaN reference compared to Samples A and A*, suggesting a larger ratio between the hopping distance and the localization length in the uncapped (Ga,Fe)N layers.

The magnetoresistance (MR) of Sample A* shows a negative slope up to a critical field, and a positive quadratic behavior at higher fields, attributed to quantum interference effects and spin-polarized hopping, respectively.

The anisotropic magnetoresistance (AMR) is observed to be positive in all samples containing the (Ga,Fe)N layers, and is one order of magnitude greater than previously reported for γ'-Fe4N thin films.
The hysteretic behavior in the MR of Sample A* at low fields, with a shift of 120 mT between up and down field sweeps, is attributed to the spin polarization of the embedded nanocrystals.

The GaN capping layer in Sample B leads to a significant increase in the resistivity, by up to three orders of magnitude at low temperatures, due to the diffusion of dilute Fe ions from the (Ga,Fe)N layer.

The FMR measurements confirm the uniaxial out-of-plane magnetic anisotropy of the γ'-GayFe4-yN nanocrystals, attributed to shape anisotropy, and the in-plane anisotropy related to the hexagonal crystal structure of the GaN matrix.
The annealing of Sample A leads to the removal of the α-Fe nanocrystals and the formation of polycrystalline FeOx at the surface, as confirmed by the XRD and TEM analyses.
The dilute Fe ions in the GaN matrix are found to occupy preferentially substitutional Ga-sites and be in the Fe3+ charge state.
The magnetization of Sample A* (annealed Sample A) shows a shift in saturation from 2T to 5T at 2K, and from 1T to 2T at room temperature, indicating the removal of the α-Fe nanocrystals.

The estimated hopping distance Rh for the Mott VRH in Sample A* is between 30-70 nm, while the localization length ξ is in the range of 7-10 nm, fulfilling the condition Rh > ξ for hopping conduction.
